subquestions.text_open: 8.2 Apply conformational analysis analogous to n-butane. 8.2.1 Rank the shown conformations of 1-butene from high to low energy.

text_images.description: 3 conformations of C=CCC. A has a left double bond and a zigzag chain ending in an ordinary vertical-up bond. B has a similar skeleton but an upward solid-wedge terminal bond. C has a solid-wedge terminal bond directed lower right.

rubric: B > A > C. (2 points; if n pairwise swaps give the correct order, award 2 - n.)

subquestions.text_open: 8.2.2 Rank the shown conformations of allyl alcohol from high to low energy.

text_images.description: 4 conformations of C=CCO. A ends in an ordinary upward OH bond; B in an upward solid-wedge OH bond; C in a rightward solid-wedge OH bond of different orientation; D ends directly in OH by an ordinary line without wedge stereochemistry.

rubric: D > B > C > A. (2 points; if n pairwise swaps give the correct order, award 2 - n.)

subquestions.text_open: 8.2.3 Rank the shown conformations of 2-methyl-1-butene from high to low energy.

text_images.description: 4 conformations of 'C=C(C)CC'. A has the terminal methyl cis to the double bond by an ordinary upward bond; B has an upward solid wedge; C a lower-right solid wedge; D an ordinary trans arrangement.

rubric: D > B > A > C. (2 points; if n pairwise swaps give the correct order, award 2 - n.)

subquestions.text_open: 8.2.4 Rank the shown conformations of methylallyl alcohol from high to low energy.

text_images.description: 4 conformations of 'C=C(C)CO'. A has OH cis to the double bond by an ordinary line; B an upward solid-wedge OH; C a rightward solid-wedge OH; D an ordinary trans double-bond/OH arrangement.

rubric: D > B > C > A. (2 points; if n pairwise swaps give the correct order, award 2 - n.)
